extracted.intended_audience: researchers, technologists, and institutions applying for Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) science funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria used by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative to evaluate and monitor grant proposals and awardees across its scientific programs (imaging, cell science, single-cell biology, open science tools/software, and related priorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI evaluates all applications for scientific merit and seeks independent expert review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions are made by CZI staff in consultation with scientific advisors; scientific merit is the primary filter applied during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with CZI scientific grand challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantmaking is aligned with CZI's four scientific grand challenges: Imaging, Cell Science, Single Cell Biology, and Open Science Tools/Software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that address one or more of these areas are prioritized as part of CZI's strategic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority focus areas (AI and education)
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI focuses its grantmaking on the use of artificial intelligence in biomedicine, technology and biomedical research driven by generative AI, and K-12 education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing emphasis on AI/ML applications; proposals leveraging AI for biomedical problems or generative-AI–driven research are of special interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA-specific requirements and evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Open competitions (RFAs) include information on the opportunity, project requirements, eligibility, application process, and specific evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow each RFA's stated project requirements and will be evaluated according to the specific criteria published with that RFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value to the biomedical community (EOSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Open Source Software for Science (EOSS) program, reviewers evaluate the value to the biomedical community of proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the software meaningfully benefits biomedical researchers and addresses community needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing adoption among biomedical researchers (EOSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess how the output will advance adoption among biomedical researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider plans, outreach, documentation, and integrations that will increase uptake by the target user base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical value to researchers' work (EOSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the value the work will produce for biomedical researchers' day-to-day work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for demonstrable ways the tool/software improves researchers’ productivity, accuracy, or capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses unmet biomedical user needs (EOSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposal addresses unmet biomedical user needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific user gaps the project will fill and evidence of demand or requirements gathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements/integration to improve adoption/usability/functionality/performance (EOSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate improvements or integration with other tools that will improve adoption, usability, functionality, or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical compatibility, APIs, performance benchmarks, and UX improvements are relevant evidence for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of intermediate outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI evaluates progress and impact through the delivery of intermediate outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are expected to produce tangible interim deliverables that demonstrate ongoing progress toward goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting and continued funding contingent on reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports must be submitted and approved to ensure continued delivery of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, substantive annual reports describing progress are required; failure to deliver acceptable reports can affect continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of awardee's research program progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must describe progress in their research program as part of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress narratives should connect intermediate outputs to overall program goals and planned future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary investigators and cross-institution collaboration (CZ Biohub)
rubrics_metrics.description: CZ Biohub programs recruit interdisciplinary investigators and value collaboration across institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals demonstrating cross-disciplinary teams and institutional collaboration are encouraged for Biohub-style funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative imaging tools and collaborative team grants (Imaging Hardware)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaging Hardware funding targets innovative imaging tools and supports collaborative team grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale, technical imaging tool proposals that involve team-based development and deployment are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell atlas projects and methodology development (Single Cell Biology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single Cell Biology programs support cell atlas projects and methodology development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals advancing single-cell methods or contributing to cell atlasing efforts are aligned with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary teams for neurodegeneration research
rubrics_metrics.description: Neurodegeneration Initiative funds multi-disciplinary teams tackling neurodegenerative disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team science that brings complementary expertise to bear on neurodegeneration is favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted partnerships for pediatric cancer research
rubrics_metrics.description: Pediatric Cancer work is conducted through a partnership with AACR focusing on childhood and adolescent cancers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligned proposals or collaborative projects with partners like AACR are appropriate for this program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Science Diversity Leadership Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Science Diversity Leadership Award targets senior URM (underrepresented minority) faculty, providing $1.15M over 5 years (through HHMI partnership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility/award structure for fostering leadership among senior URM faculty; applicants should meet the award-specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on tools, infrastructure, and open science
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI places heavy emphasis on funding tools, infrastructure, and open science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that create broadly useful infrastructure or open-source tools are particularly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value placed on cross-cutting interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-cutting interdisciplinary work is valued by CZI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects spanning disciplines and enabling new interactions across fields are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and agility in funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI emphasizes speed and agility, making faster decisions than typical public funders like NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can expect a faster review/decision timeline; proposals may be structured for iterative or rapid support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-private partnerships welcomed
rubrics_metrics.description: Public/private partnerships are welcomed by CZI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations between academic, industry, and other non-profit partners are acceptable and may strengthen proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of ambitious 'moonshot' thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambitious 'moonshot' thinking is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-risk, high-reward projects with far-reaching potential impact are within CZI's appetite—particularly when aligned with program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced emphasis on individual investigator track record compared with NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: Compared with NIH, CZI places less emphasis on the individual investigator's track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While competence and capability matter, CZI weighs other factors (tools, infrastructure, early-stage potential) more heavily than an established PI publication record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to early-stage and high-risk work
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI is more open to early-stage and high-risk work than some traditional funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that propose exploratory approaches or that lack extensive preliminary data may still be competitive if they align with CZI priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI offers more flexibility in deliverables compared with some traditional funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements may allow for adaptable milestones and outputs rather than rigid, predetermined deliverables.
